core.sync.note: client.events (license, config, updateAvailable, packs) as one SharedFlow, config.setting(key) handles (value, source, locked, visibility, set, clear, on, flow) and config.changes; on Android PolarisKeyLifecycle syncs on foreground (throttled; ETags and backoff apply). A periodic background sync is the host's WorkManager worker (no WorkManager dependency). SP-51: every licence transition emits (LiveStateTest), a revoked foreground licence shows the activation screen (RevokedInForegroundTest), and close() ends a JVM main (CloseTest).

core.store.note: Android: :android's AndroidKeystoreStore, the token and device id wrapped by :platform's SecureStore (an AndroidKeyStore AES-256-GCM key, StrongBox where present), the verified cache in a noBackup file; a FileStore's token and device id migrate in, a failed Keystore call throws and status() reports keyring-error, a lost key drops the token and keeps the device id (AndroidKeystoreStoreTest). JVM desktop (UK-40): :core's KeyringStore, Python's KeyringStore ported (the token in the OS keyring, Keychain, Credential Manager or Secret Service through java-keyring, service pkey:<product>; a verified write, else the 0600 file with status() saying keyring-error; file-first reads; a FileStore token moves in), wired by PolarisKeyDesktop in the polaris-key-desktop artifact, which brings java-keyring at runtime (SP-50); the storage contract runs against the real OS keyring on macOS, Windows and Linux in the kotlin-desktop CI matrix (KeyringStoreTest, PolarisKeyDesktopTest). java-keyring is compileOnly in :core: without it, or with no reachable keyring (a headless Linux session with no Secret Service), the token stays in the 0600 file, supports() reports dependency, as it does for a plain FileStore, and the store warns once per run (DegradedStoreWarningTest). On Android a client built without a store is refused invalid-options, never a FileStore under an empty user.home (StartedClientTest, AndroidRuntimeTest).

core.copy.note: im.plrs.key.core.Copy serves the generated Copy.generated.kt tables (from copy.en.json): message(code)/title(code) read COPY_CODES, then COPY_GATE, then COPY_ACTIVATION; activationMessage/activationTitle read COPY_ACTIVATION only (any kind spelling); an unknown code reads COPY_FALLBACK naming it; {name} placeholders fill from params or drop; registerLocale("en", ...) is the host override layer and other locales fall back to English (CopyTest checks every table against copy.en.json). The Android kit's PolarisCopy keeps its own fields (host overrides and string resources still win) and reads Copy.message for every other refusal code the catalog knows (PolarisCopyMappingTest).

core.backend.note: client.backend (im.plrs.key.sdk.BackendClient): install(OkHttpClient.Builder) adds interceptor() (origin check, pre-sync, one forced retry at least 10 s after the last, typed not_entitled/sign_in_required) and networkInterceptor() (every hop's origin checked before it is sent, then X-PKey-License and X-PKey-Device attached; an application interceptor alone attaches nothing); headers() is raw. backendOrigins: exact, https except loopback. ClientBackendMatrixTest replays backend-matrix.json's client rows; BackendTest covers the rest.

license.manage.note: PX-W8: the device-limit result exposes manageUrl (validated), plus the return and key helpers.

license.refusals.note: ActivationResult's typed refusals by the body's code, each carrying the registry code (LicenseEndpoints, LicenseClientTest); the activate-refusals transcript replays.

config.mirror.note: The Kotlin mirror is rendered by tools/gen-mirrors.ts (--lang kotlin); the :config tests compile the committed sample.

config.local.note: config.set/clear/clearAll persist device-local overrides in local-config.json beside the store, checked against the catalog (or the document's type), never over an enforced or hidden entry (managed_by_admin); config.setting(key) handles (value, source, locked, visibility, set, clear, on, flow) and config.changes emit every change (ConfigLocalTest, ConfigSettingTest).

config.sync.note: client.config.set/clear/setting route a synced key through the Cloud Sync machine while a person is signed in (ConfigSyncPort); setting(key).sync() answers local, pending or synced, and ConfigChange.origin names local, remote, merge or migration. CloudSyncSettingsTest and SyncScenariosTest settingCases.

devices.fingerprint.note: :core derives fingerprints and device ids from supplied inputs (every fingerprint.json section in :conformance); on Android :android's AndroidFingerprintSource reads ANDROID_ID (else a random anchor kept in the Keystore), Build.MODEL and the RAM bucket, checked against the corpus vectors, ramBuckets and deviceIds (AndroidFingerprintTest).

devices.facts.note: JvmDeviceFactsSource reads a JVM desktop; :android's AndroidDeviceFactsSource reads Build and answers the product's declared android probes one package at a time through PackageManager (no enumeration; AndroidFactsTest).

devices.report.note: PolarisKeyClient.report(): the facts, the verified config and entitlement values, caps, content.packSetId, gate {status}, outlet, and the update-health journal (`updates`, at most 16 per report, marked sent once accepted; notes/SDK-PARITY-PASS.md §3.13). UpdateClient journals update_offered, the boot guard update_applied, update_reverted, boot_rolled_back and update_confirmed, PacksClient update_downloaded, update_applied and pack_failed, and both Android install drivers update_downloaded and update_applied (UpdateEventJournalTest, BootGuardEventsTest, DevicesTest, DirectInstallDriverTest).

telemetry.updates.note: The update-health journal rides devices/report, at most 16 events per report, dropped once accepted (UpdateEventJournalTest, DevicesTest); the telemetry-report-updates transcript replays.

devices.attest.note: client.devices.attest() (:core's attestDevice): POST devices/attest/challenge, the platform token for the requestHash, POST devices/attest, the Worker's refusal codes kept. On Android :android's PlayIntegrityAttestation over :platform's PlatformIntegrity (the challenge's cloud project number, or AndroidOptions.playCloudProjectNumber); a direct build, or a play build Google Play did not install, answers outlet. Attest-and-retry (one attest, one retry on attestation_required) on edge-mint and commerce claims (AttestTest, PlayIntegrityAttestationTest). A JVM desktop build answers runtime (NoAttestation).

identity.oidc.note: Only through a host-supplied sign-in closure, as in Swift; no work package gives the Kotlin SDK its own browser sign-in (P6-07).

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: normalizeDeviceLabel over code points, CoreOptions.deviceName and defaultDeviceName (the JVM host name without .local/.lan/.home; on Android Settings.Global.DEVICE_NAME, else Build.MODEL, from the :android glue), on signIn.start, activation and registration; SignInPrompt.deviceName is the echo, and PolarisSignIn shows it under the countdown.

identity.toggle.note: I-10b.17: identity.signIn.start(SignInOptions) returns a SignInSession (wait, wait(once), cancel, reopen; Futures signInStart/signInWait); a refusal is a typed SignInError; the subject is stored through core.setSubject on signedIn; beginSignIn, pollSignIn and waitForSignIn are removed.

identity.attach.note: I-10b.16: IdentityClient.attach(confirm) (and PolarisKeyFutures.attach) over discovery's identity fragment: AttachResult.Confirm (preview, nothing written), Ok (token rotated and stored, subject, attached), Refused (the Worker's code and status; the token stays) and Unavailable; identity-attach and identity-attach-errors replayed.

identity.account.note: I-10b.15: IdentityClient.subject(), signOut() (pre-sign-out hooks, released drops the token) and openAccount(), over discovery's identity fragment; PolarisEvent.Identity; BootResult.subject; identity-subject-signout and discovery-identity transcripts replayed.

identity.redirect.web.note: I-10b.18: signIn.start(SignInOptions(channel = Redirect, redirectUri)) builds the S256 authorize URL from discovery (IdentityRedirect) for a browser the host opens; session.complete(callbackUrl) checks the redirect URI, state and iss before anything is sent, then redeems the code at discovery's token endpoint (form body, product origin only). Single use; a refusal is a typed SignInError and never wipes the token. Loopback, scheme and claimed-HTTPS redirects are I-15's; the licence choice (license_choice=app) is I-10b.19's.

identity.choice.note: I-10b.19: identity.choice.licenses/devices/complete/cancel over the endpoints discovery names (typed service-unavailable N/A otherwise), no bearer, the grant never in an error; a Worker refusal is ChoiceResult.Refused (retryAfterSeconds, manageUrl, signInUrl, keyEntries, the fresh view); Keep completes attachable. The three choice-* transcripts are replayed.

identity.exchange.note: I-45.1/I-45.3: identity.exchangeNonce/exchange over the endpoints discovery names (Unavailable otherwise; a Worker refusal throws PolarisException); the nine exchange transcripts are replayed. The Credential Manager provider is I-45.4; JVM desktop has no platform identity.

identity.gamecenter.note: Game Center exists only on Apple platforms.

identity.pgs.note: Play Games server auth code (I-45.5); JVM desktop has none.

identity.autosignin.note: autoSignIn() rungs 1-4 (plan-auto-sign-in §1, I-45): a stored sign-in, the platform provider silently, then its one sheet; every refusal is a result.

identity.keyentry.note: I-10b.14: ActivationResult.Ok.keyEntries, KeyEntryLimit(manageUrl, keyEntries) and LicenseOwned(signInUrl); keyentry-* transcripts replayed.

release.download.note: installUrl()/downloadUrl() build the transcript-pinned URLs; release.fetch(target, to, onProgress) downloads one build of a VERIFIED release record from discovery's builds template (Distribution's, else Release's) with the bearer and X-PKey headers, in bounded Range windows resumed with If-Range, and keeps nothing unless size and SHA-256 match (DeliveryHelpersTest); distribution.downloadModel()/thisPlatform() type the public download page.

release.fetch.note: release.fetch(target, to, onProgress): the build of a verified record from discovery's builds template with the bearer, bounded Range windows (the last one open-ended) resumed with If-Range, nothing kept unless size and SHA-256 match (DeliveryHelpersTest); the release-fetch-gated transcript replays.

release.distribution.note:
distribution.downloadModel() and thisPlatform() type GET /

/distribution/download.json (DeliveryHelpersTest); the distribution-download-model transcript replays.

update.check.note:
:update's UpdateClient.check(): GET /

/update/version with the token when held, a 403's wire code, updateAvailable by Core's Semver (UpdateClientTest).

update.feed.note: :core's verifyFeed, feedClaims, reloadFeeds and commitFeed (every feedCases vector, FeedCasesTest); UpdateClient.channelFeed() and decide() run them through runUpdateCheck, and Core keeps the feeds slice and its seq floors (the update-feed-rollback transcript). update.feedUrl(kind) and appcastUrl() expand discovery's appcast, winsparkle, velopack, appInstaller and zsync templates; a template the Worker does not advertise is the typed product N/A (DeliveryHelpersTest).

update.feeds.note: update.feedUrl(kind) and appcastUrl() over discovery's update.endpoints by feedUrlFrom; every feed-url-matrix.json row (FeedUrlMatrixTest); a missing template is the typed product N/A.

update.decide.note: :core's decideUpdate, bootDecision, resolveUpdateOutlet, rolloutBucket and runUpdateCheck (every update-matrix.json row and case, UpdateMatrixTest); UpdateClient.decide() over discovery's feed and record templates, the record fetched by hash and verified against pinnedReleaseKeys only (both update transcripts).

update.content.note: :core's feedContent, holdsOf (stampHolds), selectPackRows and decideUpdate with UpdateContentInput; runUpdateCheck runs P4-13 §2.5 steps 10–14 with the packs facet as the UpdateContentHost (every feedContentCases vector and contentRows row, ContentDecisionTest).

update.driver.note: :update's InstallDriver port; :android's PlayInstallDriver (play: In-App Updates, flexible or immediate by the decision's urgency and optionally Play's priority and staleness, completing a downloaded update, staging-aware) and DirectInstallDriver (direct: the verified record's one payload downloaded to private storage, size and SHA-256 checked, then :platform's verified PackageInstaller session, every refusal surfaced as swap-refused), against FakeAppUpdateManager and an installer fake (PlayInstallDriverTest, DirectInstallDriverTest); the flavour boundary holds (tools/check_flavours.sh). A Play flexible update reports its download and finishes with a restart (ProgressiveInstallDriver: progress, finish, resume). JVM desktop (UK-40): :update's DesktopInstallDriver, the default UpdateClient.install uses on a JVM and PolarisKeyDesktop wires: the verified record's one payload for the decision's build, fetched resumably by OkHttpArtifactFetch (the minimal fetch until SP-K13's release.fetch; the bearer kept to the control plane's origin), size and SHA-256 checked before the OS opens it (open, ShellExec, xdg-open or an AppImage run), a mismatch opening nothing (DesktopInstallDriverTest); UpdateClient.install journals update_applied when it hands off (§3.13). UK-10.9: DesktopInstallDriver is an InstallProgressSource (Downloading bytes, then Idle or Failed) that the kit's update prompt follows; the verification and the hand-off are unchanged (DesktopInstallDriverTest). The internal-track and self-update device runs are the owner's (P6-12 brief).

update.bootguard.note: :update's BootGuard over the host's UpdateSlots port (Godot P3-10's semantics: apply-staged and roll-back with skipVersion, failedBoots counted while an applied update is active, the stage-matrix v2 confirmation rows; BootGuardTest); the launch decision is stage-matrix.json's guard and confirm rows (StageMatrixTest). The default JVM slots (UK-40): DirUpdateSlots (staged, current and previous directories swapped by renames that recover from an interruption) and FileBootGuardStore, wired by PolarisKeyDesktop.bootGuard (DirUpdateSlotsTest). With no slots (a platform-installed Android app) nothing is counted.

outlet.detect.note: :core's detectOutlet passes every outlet-matrix.json row in :conformance; on Android :android's AndroidOutletSignalReader turns :platform's InstallSource into android.installSource and android.installerMismatch, and every Android row of the matrix replays through it (AndroidOutletTest). A JVM desktop observes no signal (NoOutletSignals): detection falls to the stamp.

crash.tags.note: client.crashTags(): release app@<version>[+<build>], environment the channel, pkey.outlet when known, as the Worker's Sentry hook reads them (DeliveryHelpersTest).

packs.record.note: :core's verifyReleaseRecord with pin.kind and :packs' verifyMarker and matchEmbedded (every packRecordCases and markerCases vector, PackRecordTest).

packs.revoke.note: :core's revocationOf, verifyRevocation and newerRevocation (every revocationCases vector); PackEngine keeps the sibling revocations.json (revocationsStored first, never created empty, re-verified per entry on load, relearn, the 256-target cap, torn and unreadable rules) and refuses and unmounts revoked releases (PackEngineTest).

packs.delegation.note: :core's delegated verifyReleaseRecord path (steps 13 and 16), verifyDelegation and recordRevoked; :packs' dataOnlyRefusal (every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector, DelegationTest); the engine fetches delegations within MAX_DELEGATIONS_PER_CHECK, refuses non-data-only delegated installs and keeps PackInstall.delegation (PackEngineTest).

packs.delta.feed.note: :core's feedContent reads the feed's deltas menu; :packs' withFeedDeltas merges it before planTarget, and PackEngine tries at most one feed-offered delta per install, falling back on a failed fetch or any delta verdict and journalling it as feedDelta; the update client hands each committed feed's menu to the packs facet (feedContentCases, feedDeltaCases, feedDeltaApplyCases, PackEngineTest).

packs.plan.note: :packs' plan, selectVariant and planTarget (every plan-matrix.json row, variant case and target case, PlanMatrixTest).

packs.index.files.note: :packs' parseFilesIndex, checkPaths and treeDigest (filesIndexCases and pathCases, ContentCorpusTest).

packs.index.chunks.note: :packs' parseChunkIndex and parseChunkIndexBytes (u64 from two little-endian u32 reads composed byte by byte, saturated at 2^53; chunkIndexCases under both zstd paths, ContentCorpusTest).

packs.apply.full.note: applyFull, streamed through zstd-jni's ZstdInputStream (and one-shot without it); applyCases under both paths.

packs.apply.file.note: applyFile with the type-neutral container rebuild; applyCases under both paths.

packs.apply.chunk.note: applyChunk (seed map, chunkRuns, repair pass, run journal resume) over chunkRangeFetch: one bounded Range per run with If-Range and Accept-Encoding identity, an exact Content-Range and ETag, never multi-range; seed indexes under <packs root>/index/ (applyCases, ContentCorpusTest).

except.note: Without the opt-in pack decoder, or where zstd-jni's native libzstd cannot load: an app adds polaris-key-zstd, whose Android variant is zstd-jni's AAR (1.5.7-12, 16 KB aligned: later AARs need compileSdk 37; SP-50), and supports() reports dependency without it (AndroidRuntimeTest on the emulator lane).
Without the opt-in pack decoder (polaris-key-zstd, whose JVM variant is zstd-jni's JAR; SP-50), or where zstd-jni ships no native binary for the OS or arch; supports() reports dependency.

packs.apply.delta.note: zstd-jni (libzstd 1.5.7): the base as a raw-content dictionary (ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary; §2.7 rule 5's magic refusal runs first) with ZSTD_d_windowLogMax, the window check in the applier before every prefix decode; a start-up probe gates zstd-patch-from (applyCases, feedDeltaApplyCases, PackZstdTest).

packs.state.note: PackEngine over DirPackStorage in the store's data directory (never a cache directory): journal, resume with Range/If-Range, atomic pointer swap (fsync before rename), confirm, rollback, GC roots, embedded baselines, a torn state.json held aside, an unreadable one refusing every write; packSetId on devices/report (packSetIdCases, PackEngineTest).

packs.handlers.note: PackHandler (supports, check over a newly staged payload before the state commit -> pack-type-check-failed, activate with the installed payload, deactivate); files.tree, data.json and l10n.table built in; registerHandler for custom types (PackEngineTest, PackTypeHandlersTest).

packs.type.l10n.table.note: L10nTableHandler (built in): PO, CSV and JSON tables by plain parsers scanned as code points, the BCP-47 locale matched to the variant; tables(packId), onActivate/onDeactivate (pack-type-cases.json, PackTypeHandlersTest).

packs.type.data.json.note: DataJsonHandler (built in): every file strict JSON, formatVersions listed by the host; documents(packId) (pack-type-cases.json, PackTypeHandlersTest).

packs.type.ml.model.note: MlModelHandler (host-registered, as in Swift): model.json runtime, quantisation and RAM/VRAM needs against the host budget, then the host load test (TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime) before model(packId) swaps (pack-type-cases.json, PackTypeHandlersTest).

packs.provides.note: PackEngine.isAvailable over the running set and packFor over the targets, from each verified record's provides (unentitled packs never answer; PackEngineTest).

packs.transport.play.note: :android's PadPackTransport (play) over :platform's AssetPacks: the Play asset pack named by the pack id with dots and hyphens as underscores, its assetsPath re-read on every call and never persisted (pkey/ or a pkey#tcf_* directory), handed to :packs as embedded baselines that the marker, record and stamp pin verify; ensure() to COMPLETED with a confirm hook before Play's dialog. The direct build answers Unsupported (outlet). Fake-proven (PadPackTransportTest); a pack delivered mid-session mounts at the facet's next start, and the fast-follow device run is the owner's.

packs.transport.steam.note: As in Swift, no work package builds a Steam-depot transport for a JVM desktop app (P5-08 covers Godot only).

ui.stages.note: :core's bootTransition; every stage-matrix.json row, probe, guard and confirm case in :conformance.

ui.boot.note: SP-20: client.boot() in :sdk (Boot.kt, plain coroutines, no Android): BootDriver runs :core's stage machine over client.bootHost(): discovery when services are unpinned or no token is held, keyless registration of a fresh install under an open policy before the sync pass, the boot guard over the default update slots where present, sync, a gate that registers keylessly and syncs again when it needs activation under an open policy, decide when usable, packs.bootFetch and mount, to its first stop. :ui's PolarisBootState is a thin holder over the same driver. Proof: :conformance replays boot-cold-register.json through client.boot() and plays every stage-matrix.json row through BootDriver with a scripted host (BootDriverMatrixTest); BootDriverTest in :sdk.

ui.kit.note: Android only: there is no JVM desktop kit yet (SP-K12's Compose Multiplatform target), and the registry allows no jvm exception for ui.kit until SP-00 adds one (notes/SDK-PARITY-PASS.md SP-01). P6-11's :ui (polaris-key-ui, Jetpack Compose + Material 3, Android): PolarisKeyGate (the one-call wiring, formerly PolarisKeyApp; LocalPolarisKey and the remember* helpers), PolarisBoot over :core's stage machine, the gate (every terminal state and the grace banner), activation, sign-in with QR, settings, devices, the update banner and prompt and pack progress, each with a StateFlow state holder; neutral over the host's MaterialTheme by default, Polaris Key branding behind PolarisBranding.PolarisKey and the Powered-by badge behind showPoweredBy. Routes and deep links (UK-09b.3): PolarisKeyRoute and PolarisKeyLinks, an allow-list parser (the host's return URI plus one known route, nothing else) with PolarisKeyLinksTest as its table; PolarisKeyGateStartTest pins one client start. Responsive (UI-KITS.md §1.4, §1.5): one scaffold picks the layout from the window: a tall window top-anchors a focused step and docks its controls; sign-in and activation go two-pane at compact height, on Android TV and in wide landscape windows; message screens never split (a trailing action row, a card on TV and wide windows). Sign-in resumes the same code after rotation or navigation, leads with the QR on TV (no browser opener there; every opener guarded), and can run inside the gate. The product is the hero: the host's icon or a monogram tile, never the Pinned K outside the Powered-by badge; an optional product accent resolved against the host's own surfaces under the native preset. Proof: every screen's Roborazzi snapshots (light, dark, 200 % font, phone, tablet; neutral and branded); the responsive set at 360x640, 891x411, 640x360, 673x841, 1920x1080, 150 % font, 960x540, 1280x720, 2560x1440 and TV 960x540, plus focus-ring and accent references; ResponsiveLayoutTest (every control on screen and 48 dp tall at those sizes and 800x600, 1280x800, 1366x768, 411x440, 891x411 at 150/200 % and 640x360 at 150 %); FlowTest; the branding (dynamic colour, product accent), contrast and TalkBack suites. Desktop (UK-10.6): the GNOME (libadwaita) chrome behind the forced `Gnome` variant: 34 px controls at radius 8 with a pill suggested action, an AdwDialog for the update sheet (radius 12, soft shadow, 7 % edge in light), AdwStatusPage message screens, an AdwAlertDialog for Replace (responses side by side, stacked when narrow), the portal's accent for the native preset; GnomeChromeTest asserts each rule and GnomeBoardShotsTest renders the board to PKEY_KIT_SHOTS (UK-10.12 commits the set). Desktop sizes (UK-10.11): SizeMatrixTest renders six screens in the three chromes at the seven §7.1 window sizes (the Mac at its 480 x 520 floor, scrolling below it), font scale 2 at 390x844, 844x390 and 1440x900, and touch at 390x844, asserting no control clipped, no cut text, no sideways scroll, the primary action in the first viewport and targets of 24 dp (mouse) or 44 dp (touch); PresetIdentityContrastTest covers a fake presentation source (accent and icon, no integrator code), every §3.1 theme field, label contrast measured on the render for #ff6a3d and a dark accent, and high contrast (GNOME reads the portal) and reduced transparency rendering opaque. Desktop windows (UK-10.8, K3): ApplicationScope composables in the OS frame: PolarisKeyWindow (the gate window; every close goes to the host's onCloseRequest, exit by default; a mandatory update is a dialog inside it with no close; the Mac sheet floats 52 dp down only with fullSizeContent, else 12 dp; the Mac window's minimumSize is 480 x 520), PolarisUpdateWindow (an optional update: one 440 dp column, not resizable, sized to its content), PolarisSettingsWindow (650 dp, the pane named in the title, Escape or the OS close button closes it, no Done) and PolarisMenuItems for MenuBar (Check for updates, Manage license; the macos variants on macOS; Sign out only there and in Settings, Account). DesktopWindowsTest covers the state holders, the menu labels and the contents laid out offscreen.

commerce.receipt.note: client.commerce (:sdk's CommerceClient, P6-01): binding() and claim(store, payload) with claimPlay, claimSteam and claimAppStore, ClaimResult Ok / NotOwned / AttestationRequired / Refused(code, reason) (the host syncs after an Ok claim, as the transcript pins), attest-and-retry on attestation_required, hiddenHere/isUnlocked (App Store 3.1.3(b)); the commerce-claim transcript replays. Steam claims work on the JVM (the host passes the GetAuthTicketForWebApi hex ticket); Play Billing's one-call purchase and restore are :billing's PolarisPlayBilling in polaris-key-billing (obfuscatedAccountId = the binding, claim, acknowledge after the claim).

sync.scenarios.note: conformance SyncScenariosTest drives settingCases and every sync-scenarios.json scenario through :core's CloudSyncMachine, on the JCA and on Tink.

sync.settings.note: client.cloudSync.status()/flush()/newRecoveryCode() (and statusFuture/flushFuture on PolarisKeyFutures) and PolarisEvent.CloudSync on client.events (sdk/CloudSyncApi.kt): one machine per client over the key ring, driven by identity subject changes, with the discovery gate and the typed N/A while the product has no Sync service. The sign-out chain is Connect stop and leave, a bounded flush with the root held, ring forget (a failure stops the sign-out), machine sign-out, purge; a person change never flushes under the new token. State is cloud-sync.json in the store's state directory (noBackupFilesDir on Android). PolarisKeyLifecycle flushes (bounded) when the last activity stops. CloudSyncSettingsTest, CloudSyncHostTest, CloudSyncHostBoundsTest, CloudSyncTransportOkHttpTest and the cloudsync-* transcripts in TranscriptTest.

sync.keyring.note: client.keyring (:sdk's SyncKeyring, over :core's im.plrs.key.core.sync: JCA HKDF, HMAC and AES-GCM, RFC 9180 mode_base written out over DeviceKeyPort.dh for open and an ephemeral X25519 key from DeviceCurves for seal, so it runs on Tink below Android API 33): create(), unlock() (opens this device's wrap through the port's dh, so the agreement key never leaves the store), wrapTo()/removeWrap(), setRecoveryCode()/recover(), reset()/adopt()/openAdopted(), acceptRingChange(confirmed), attach(listener) feeding setRoot, and the codec. The first root pins {ringId, epoch, rootKid} per product (a file in the state directory, memory without one); a served ring that differs is RingChanged and is never opened. The root is also kept in one record that is used only while it matches the pin: on the JVM the owner-only 0600 file pkey.sync-root.v1.bin beside the device keys (the JVM has no OS keyring; memory only without a state directory, which status().rootPersistence reports), on Android a Keystore-sealed file under its own alias (androidSyncRootStorage, never backed up). forget() drops the root and the pin and runs from the sign-out hook after Connect leaves (a delete that fails stops the sign-out). Every type holding key material prints as redacted. SyncVectorsTest (hkdf, envelope, blind, canonicalJson, hpkeAnchor, wrap, recovery and adopt cases, on the JCA and on Tink), SyncKeyringTest and the keyring-* transcripts in TranscriptTest.

connect.identity.note: Verification is :core's Peer (verifyCert, verifyRing, replaceRing, admitPeer); :conformance's PeerCasesTest drives peerCertCases, ringCases (the ring-lifetime-* rows included) and peerAdmissionCases on JCA and on Tink (CC-12.1). client.connect (:sdk, ConnectTest) makes the device keys on first need, registers them (registerDeviceKeys, PUT devices/keys), fetches GET connect/identity, verifies the roster and certificate against the effective set, refuses a stale, foreign, expired or other-keys answer, and holds them with K_disc as pkey.connect.v1 (owner-only file beside the device keys; memory-only keys refuse unless allowEphemeralKeys; an unreadable key record is an error); the previous K_disc is dropped after a leave or a key change; listDevices() and leave() (also run before sign-out). Android supplies its Keystore-sealed key store and state storage (CC-12b). No connect-identity transcript is recorded yet, so none is replayed.

connect.noise.note: Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 in :core (peer.Noise) on DeviceCurves, so it runs on JCA and on Tink (API 24 to 32); :conformance replays noise-vectors.json on both.

connect.protocol.note: pkey-peer/1 in :core: adverts, prologue, PSK, SAS, frames, records and the PeerChannel and PeerLink engines (modes a, v, p; commit-reveal SAS, handshake limits, write cap); :conformance replays peer-matrix.json, with :core's PeerChannelTest, PeerChannelSasTest and PeerLinkTest.

connect.lan.note: The JVM half is built and tested: :core mDNS (JvmMdns, bounded tables, per-source caps) and TCP pipes, and :sdk ConnectLan, used off Android (ConnectLanTest, the live test under PKEY_LIVE_MDNS=1). Android has no adapter yet, so LAN reports off with reason unsupported there and the relay still works; CC-12b adapts :platform NSD to the MdnsAdapter and PeerPipe ports, adds the ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK permission (nearby-permission-denied) and the Keystore-sealed state storage.

connect.relay.note: client.connect.relayTicket() and :sdk's ConnectRelay (ticket offer, WebSocket on an OkHttp client with interceptors cleared and the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol echo checked, reconnect policy, LIMIT and close codes, mode-a relay sessions, pacing); ConnectRelayTest and ConnectRelaySessionTest. Works on the JVM and on Android.
